message.content:
## Verdict
You cannot certify tenant isolation with these documents. The Permission Model page states it "does not protect against malicious code" and "does not provide security guarantees in the presence of malicious code"; it is a "seat belt" against mistakes in trusted code ([#permissions](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permissions)). SECURITY.md likewise treats "the code it is asked to run" as trusted and lists `--permission` as blast-radius reduction, "not … a security boundary against intentional misuse" ([Permission Model Boundaries](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nodejs/node/v24.21.0/SECURITY.md)).

## Assumptions requiring change
1. **`--allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js` is wider than it looks.** "After passing a wildcard character (`*`) all subsequent characters will be ignored. For example: `/home/*.js` will work similar to `/home/*`" ([File System Permissions](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#file-system-permissions)).
2. **`--env-file` is a documented, intended exception**, not a controlled read: such flags "read files before environment initialization … are not subject to the rules of the Permission Model" ([constraints](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permission-model-constraints)). It can also carry `NODE_OPTIONS`, which is allowed to include permission flags ([NODE_OPTIONS](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/cli.html#node_optionsoptions)).
3. **The pre-opened descriptor bypasses the model**: "Using existing file descriptors via the `node:fs` module bypasses the Permission Model" ([constraints](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#permission-model-constraints)).
4. **Relative symlinks are a documented break**: "Symbolic links will be followed even to locations outside of the set of paths that access has been granted to. … you must ensure that no paths to which access has been granted contain relative symbolic links" ([Limitations](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#limitations-and-known-issues)). Fix before deploy.
5. **Worker inheritance is UNVERIFIED — the sources conflict.** The constraints list says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread"; SECURITY.md says workers inherit the parent's restrictions and that modified `execArgv` grants nothing extra; `worker_threads` docs say `execArgv` is inherited by default ([Worker options](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/worker_threads.html#new-workerfilename-options)). Resolve by reading v24.21.0 source/tests (e.g. `lib/internal/permission.js`, worker permission tests); do not assume "exactly the parent's restrictions".
6. **Uncovered surface.** PM restricts only fs, child process, workers, WASI, addons, OpenSSL STORE and own-inspector — not network. `process._debugProcess()` is "not gated by the `kInspector` scope or any other" and can force same-user Node processes to open the Inspector ([that section](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#process_debugprocess-and-cross-process-inspector-activation)). Workers also share the process address space, so they are never a tenant boundary.

## Useful for trusted code
Production `--permission` (enforce); `--permission-audit` only to discover needed grants, since it never denies and `--permission` overrides it ([audit](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/cli.html#--permission-audit)); `process.permission.has/drop` to narrow scopes after init — `drop()` does not close open fds, children or workers ([runtime API](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.21.0/docs/api/permissions.html#runtime-api)). Add OS-level isolation (separate UID, containers/seccomp/AppArmor) as the actual tenant boundary.

I have enough. Note the conflicting worker inheritance: permissions.html constraints says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." SECURITY.md says workers inherit permission restrictions of parent; worker_threads.html says non-process-specific options inherited by default (execArgv inherited by default). So the docs conflict. I should state limitation: the CLI/docs do not establish one consistent answer.

Wait — which is authoritative for v24.21.0? permissions.html says "does not inherit to a worker thread" (implying worker threads have no restrictions, i.e., you need --allow-worker to even create them, and once created, they're not restricted?). SECURITY.md (v24.21.0 tag) says workers inherit. Conflicting. Mark UNVERIFIED; resolving evidence target: the Node.js source at v24.21.0 (lib/internal/permission.js / worker implementation) or an issue/PR; also note as a security policy statement, does inheriting matter for vulnerability treatment.

Now the key points for the answer:

1. Premise correction: Permission Model is not a tenant-isolation boundary — docs state it doesn't protect against malicious code, malicious code can bypass it and execute arbitrary code; SECURITY.md treats code as trusted and says the model reduces blast radius of mistakes in trusted app code. So "sole tenant-isolation boundary" is invalid. Cannot certify tenant isolation.

2. --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js: wildcard semantics — after a wildcard, subsequent characters ignored, so /srv/jobs/*.js behaves like /srv/jobs/* — grants the whole /srv/jobs tree, not just *.js. Silently wider than intended.

3. --env-file reads before permission model init → not subject to permission rules; means the env file out-of-list read works as they observed, and is an intentional documented exception (not a bypass you can control for untrusted code — but note env can set NODE_OPTIONS etc.). Also OpenSSL config, V8 flags via v8.setFlagsFromString.

4. Already-open fd passed to the job: documented "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model." So the fd is a full read (and if writable, write) channel ignoring the fs allowlist.

5. Relative symlinks: documented limitation — symlinks followed to outside granted paths; must ensure granted paths contain no relative symlinks. Their premise is confirmed as a real problem. Also SECURITY.md says symlinks resolving to allowed paths is intended, TOCTOU within allowlist isn't a bypass — so path resolution is realpath-based on the *allowed* side, but relative links in the granted tree undermine it.

6. --allow-worker + assumption workers inherit exactly parent's restrictions: conflicting evidence (UNVERIFIED above). Also --allow-worker doesn't restrict what a worker can do beyond that.

7. --permission-audit does not deny; if both given, --permission wins. So staging audit-mode drift: audit doesn't test the enforce behavior; but note the audit flag doesn't require --permission.

8. Useful for trusted application code: seat belt — catch accidental fs/spawn/worker access, runtime process.permission.has / drop to narrow after init; audit mode for discovering needed permissions; note drop() doesn't close already-open resources.

9. Other gaps: process._debugProcess() not gated — sandboxed process with no grants can signal another Node.js process of same OS user to open Inspector; mitigation OS-level per docs. Also fs access via other means (node:sqlite) not guaranteed blocked; OpenSSL STORE broad; native addons/WASI need explicit allow.

Answer: which assumptions require changing:
- sole tenant-isolation boundary (must change; add OS/VM isolation)
- /srv/jobs/*.js grants whole tree
- --env-file read outside allowlist works (documented exception, keep but know env vars reach process)
- passed fd bypasses PM
- relative symlinks in granted tree must be eliminated
- worker inheritance claim: unresolved conflict → don't rely on it; verify with source/tests
Recommendations: enforce mode in prod; audit for permission discovery only; use process.permission.drop() after init; treat PM as seat belt, use containers/seccomp/separate UID per tenant; disable network? Not in PM scope at all — note PM doesn't restrict network by default (not mentioned as restricted: the list is fs, child process, workers, WASI, addons, OpenSSL store, inspector). So network egress is unrestricted → big tenant isolation gap. Good point: documented list of restricted permissions doesn't include network.

Also worker threads share memory in-process — same address space; not an isolation boundary between tenants regardless.
